## CodeRabbit — "State of AI vs Human Code Generation" (December 2025) [5]

**Sample:** 470 open-source GitHub pull requests

**Findings by vulnerability type:**
- AI code 2.74x more likely to add XSS vulnerabilities [5]
- AI code 1.91x more likely to make insecure object references [5]
- AI code 1.88x more likely to introduce improper password handling [5]
- AI code 1.82x more likely to implement insecure deserialization [5]
- Logic and correctness issues rose 75% [5]
- Excessive I/O operations ~8x more common in AI-authored PRs [5]

**Where humans performed worse:**
- Human PRs had 1.76x more spelling errors [5]
- Human code had 1.32x more testability issues [5]

## Veracode — 2025 GenAI Code Security Report [6]

**Sample:** 100+ LLMs, 4 programming languages, 80 coding tasks

**Overall finding:** AI-generated code contains 2.74x more vulnerabilities than human-written code [6]

**Failure rate by CWE:**

| CWE | Vulnerability Type | Insecure Code Rate |
|-----|-------------------|-------------------|
| CWE-80 | Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) | 86% insecure [6] |
| CWE-117 | Log Injection | 88% insecure [6] |
| CWE-89 | SQL Injection | 20% insecure (80% secure) [6] |

**Overall secure coding benchmark failure rate:** 45% [6]

## Apiiro — Fortune 50 Enterprise Research (September 2025) [7]

**Context:** Research across Fortune 50 enterprise repositories

**Findings:**
- By June 2025, AI-generated code was introducing over 10,000 new security findings per month — a 10x spike in just six months compared to December 2024 [7]
- 322% more privilege escalation paths [7]
- 153% more design flaws [7]
- 40% jump in secrets exposure [7]

## Georgetown CSET — Issue Brief (November 2024) [8]

**Authors:** Jessica Ji, Jenny Jun, Maggie Wu, Rebecca Gelles

**Three categories of risk identified:**
1. Models generating insecure code [8]
2. Models themselves being vulnerable to attack and manipulation [8]
3. Downstream cybersecurity impacts (feedback loops in training future AI systems) [8]

**Methodology:** Evaluated 5 LLMs against MITRE Top 25 CWE list using ESBMC formal verification tool. Safety properties tested included out-of-bounds array access, illegal pointer dereferences, integer overflows, undefined behavior on shift operations, floating-point NaN, and divide by zero [8].

**Finding:** All five models tested demonstrated a tendency to produce similar — and severe — bugs. High rate of unsuccessful verification across all models [8].

**Policy recommendation:** The burden of ensuring AI-generated code is secure should not rest solely on individual users, but also on AI developers, organizations producing code at scale, and policymaking bodies [8].

## Language-Level Vulnerability Rates [18]

From aggregated research across multiple studies:

| Language | Vulnerability Rate Range |
|----------|------------------------|
| Python | 16.18% - 18.50% |
| JavaScript | 8.66% - 8.99% |

"This suggests a stronger influence on vulnerabilities by language characteristics than by the AI system itself." [18]

## Mitigation Effectiveness [18]

| Technique | Effect |
|-----------|--------|
| FDSP (iterative static analyzer feedback) | Reduced vulnerability rate from 40.2% to 7.4% for GPT-4 [18] |
| Security reminders in system prompts | Part of 73.3% average remediation success [18] |
| Real-time detection feedback | GPT-4.1 achieved 96.8% remediation success rate [18] |
| ProSec (proactive alignment) | Up to 35% reduction in vulnerability rate [18] |

**Progress over time:** Comparison of October 2024 vs September 2025 experiments shows overall detection and remediation rates improving from ~50% to ~75-80% [18].

---

## Gaps and Limitations

- CodeRabbit and Veracode both report a 2.74x figure — this may be coincidence, shared methodology, or one citing the other. The provenance of this convergence was not established.
- Apiiro's 10x figure represents total monthly findings volume, which conflates increased AI code adoption with per-unit vulnerability rates.
- Most industry reports come from security vendors with commercial interest in highlighting AI code risks.
- The 12-65% non-compliance range from aggregated studies [18] is extremely wide, reflecting fundamental differences in methodology, task difficulty, and what counts as a "vulnerability."
- Georgetown CSET is a policy brief, not a peer-reviewed study.
